Issued at 1204 PM MDT Wed Oct 28 2026

There is currently dry, zonal flow aloft over southern Idaho.
Also, currently there is an upper level low centered just off 
the coast of central British Columbia with another upper level 
low centered off the coast of central California. These upper
level lows will drive the weather/precipitation over the
upcoming weekend.

Today will be dry as we transition from zonal flow aloft to 
southwesterly flow aloft. Highs today will be very similar to 
yesterday, generally in the mid 40s to low 50s. Wind gusts today
will be around 25 mph across the Arco Desert/INL and around 15 
to 20 mph elsewhere. 

The bulk of Thursday will also be dry as temperatures warm just
a few degrees with southwesterly flow aloft. Thursday morning
look for patchy fog, especially in lower elevations near water
sources. Expect temperatures in the low to mid 50s for most 
lower elevations on Thursday. Look for overall light winds 
Thursday too.

By very late Thursday night or very early Friday morning, our 
next system is just beginning to bring the start of some 
precipitation to southeastern Idaho. An area of low pressure off
the coasts of the Washington and Oregon will be just starting 
to pull in some Pacific moisture into southeastern Idaho. It is 
this low off the Oregon and Washington coasts that moves inland 
during the weekend bringing cooler air and good precipitation
chances. Deep troughing over the West will transport even more 
moisture into our area from the other upper level low over 
Southern California going into late Saturday and, especially, 
Sunday.

The current trend has been to decrease QPF on Friday, allowing 
temperatures to stay "warm" for one more day before more 
organized showers arrive for the weekend and bring a cool down. 
On Friday, the more limited precipitation we do have around will
likely favor parts of the Central Mountains. The rest of the 
higher elevations will start to receive precipitation Friday 
afternoon/evening before showers become more widespread and 
steady late Saturday into Sunday. Saturday late afternoon into
the early evening models still show a chance for 0.02 to 0.10 of
rain across lower elevations that will likely have impacts on
Halloween activities. The bulk of the precipitation is still
arriving late Saturday through Sunday and lingering into Monday
morning.  

While total QPF numbers continue to change from model 
run to model run, there currently is at least a 50-70 percent 
chance that all of our CWA across southeastern Idaho sees at 
least 0.25 inch of precipitation from Saturday morning to 
Monday morning. Plus, for some higher elevations, especially the
farther east you go, those 48-hour totals will likely be closer
to 0.75-1.50 of liquid precipitation. Temperatures will also 
drop with highs on Sunday and Monday being the low to mid 40s 
for most areas. As a result, expect better snow amounts 
especially for our northern areas (Central mountains and the 
Montana Divide) above 6500 to 7500 feet with 6 to 12 inches of 
snow likely for Central mountains (to include the Salmon river 
mountains, Sawtooth mountains, West Smokys mountains, Smoky 
mountains, White Cloud mountains, Boulder mountains, Pioneer 
mountains, White Knob mountains and the Lost river range). 
Higher elevations for the Pioneers and Big Lost range could see 
up to 18 inches of snow. Galena Summit has 12 inches of snow 
currently forecasted. Areas across the Montana Divide will see 6
to 12 inches of snow above 7000 to 7500 feet as well. The 
Eastern Highlands is a little less certain with snow levels. The
snow levels look to be higher when more precipitation moves 
through on Sunday, with snow levels around 8000 to 9000 feet. 
These areas, especially in the Wasatch Idaho mountains above 
8000 to 9000 feet, will get 6 to 12 inches of snow too.
